Here we are ! I fixed a small mistake I made both in the code and in the tests.

I could test this last fix extensively with both your project and the test scene from #61174, with various combinations of `KEEP_HEIGHT`/`KEEP_WIDTH`, viewport size and viewport size override. 
I think I finally got it right.

All this made me realize that `SubViewport.size_2d_override_stretch` doesn't work [as documented](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_subviewport.html#class-subviewport-property-size-2d-override-stretch) and should better be named `SubViewport.enable_size_2d_override`.

It actually acts as a global flag that toggles on / off the whole 2d size overriding logic - not only the stretch aspect of it.
In other words, when `size_2d_override_stretch` is `false`, `size_2d_override` is ignored everywhere.
Note that the base class' `Viewport.size_2d_override_stretch()` always return true and `Window` inherits this behavior. In those 2 classes `size_2d_override` will be effective right away.

We might want to clarify the documentation at some point.

Unit tests this PR adds that cover `FRUSTUM` camera mode now fail since this rebase.

I couldn't spend time on it yet. There are 3 possible causes:

1. Precision issues in the tests introduced by `Math::SQRT3` (which is a `constexpr double` unlike the previous local `#define SQRT3 1.732050f`)

2. A mistake I could have made doing the rebase that could have changed the tests' logic

3. A regression affecting projections in `FRUSTUM` camera mode that were introduced by another PR in the meantime

I will switch this PR to draft until it's resolved.

Now tests pass.
It was case no. 3 with `Projection::get_viewport_half_extents()` having a different behavior with non-symmetrical viewports since #100209.
